newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds make further gains on foreign bidding.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds make further gains on foreign bidding.

text.p: Irish government bonds advanced in brisk trade on Thursday as further overseas buying pushed up prices across the curve, one dealer said.
"It's been a fairly busy day with overseas investors seeing good value in the Irish market. The long papers seem to have performed best after being snapped up by bargain-hunters," one dealer said.
By 1400 GMT the eight percent bond due 2001 was up 20p at 105.37 to yield 6.36 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 rose 25p to 106.50 to yield 6.94 percent.
Dealers in Dublin said they expected a NTMA tap in the 2001 bond as there was widespread demand by investors.
In the UK, gilts extended earlier gains after lagging European markets for several days, as domestic and foreign buyers continued to pump money into the market, dealer said.

Dealers said markets may have been buoyed by German reports that Bonn plans no further Bund issues in 1996. German Bunds made gains on the news on Thursday but analysts said advances were mainly driven by futures trading and not backed up by foreign interest.
